newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS - Santer, de Silguy see EMU pact deal.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Santer, de Silguy see EMU pact deal.

text.p: The European Commission said on Friday it was confident Europe would resolve a dispute over a stability pact aimed at limiting budget deficits under monetary union.

France's new Socialist-led government said on Monday it would not approve the pact without reassurances that the EU would step up the fight against unemployment and intensify coordination of economic policies.
European Commission President Jacques Santer said Europe should be able to reach agreement, paving the way for approval of the pact at a summit in Amsterdam on Monday and Tuesday.

He told French radio a proposal by the Netherlands, which currently holds the EU presidency, would integrate a goal to boost employment into plans for more coordination of economic policies under monetary union.
He made no suggestion this would be a numerical target.
According to one French official, there would be no numerical target on jobs.

Santer said that if the European Union managed to "give muscle" to two articles in the Maastricht treaty on monetary union -- articles 102a and 103, which provide for economic policy coordination -- "we will certainly have an agreement".
"In the proposal made by the Dutch (EU) presidency, we would also integrate a jobs target in the coordination of economic policy," he said.

France's Socialist party vowed in its election campaign to push for a European economic government and to shift the focus away from austerity in monetary union towards the need for growth and employment.
European Commissioner for monetary affairs, Yves-Thibault de Silguy, also said he believed there would be a deal on the pact, which was agreed in principle in Dublin last year.

"The text that was adopted in Dublin as well as two other very important texts which are the new European monetary system and the legal status of the euro...these texts will be finally adopted in Amsterdam," de Silguy told Radio Monte Carlo.

"We will add parallel to these texts...resolutions which on the one hand give more content to the provisions that exist in the (Maastricht) treaty on employment, and secondly will also give more content to what we call the coordination of economic policy; that is to say putting in place a sort of economic pillar at the heart of economic and monetary union," he said.

French President Jacques Chirac and Prime Minister Lionel Jospin were due to hold talks on Europe on Friday with German Chancellor Helmut Kohl at a regular Franco-German summit in Poitiers, western France.
The talks were to be attended also by finance and foreign affairs ministers from both countries.
